60121435.s: Dammam Regional Museum is one of a series of museums established by the Ministry of Education under the supervision of the Deputy Ministry for Antiquities and Museums and under the patronage of Prince Mohammed bin Fahd bin Abdullah Al Saud. It opened on 24/7/1405 AH in its temporary premises on the fourth floor of the Dammam Public Library. The museum has six archaeological, heritage and natural history halls, plus the Eastern Province Emir's Hall, which opened later in 1421 AH.
60121435.b: Dammam Regional Museum is one of a series of museums established by the Ministry of Education under the supervision of the Deputy Ministry for Antiquities and Museums and under the patronage of Prince Mohammed bin Fahd bin Abdullah Al Saud. It opened on 24/7/1405 AH in its temporary premises on the fourth floor of the Dammam Public Library. The museum has six archaeological, heritage and natural history halls, plus the Eastern Province Emir's Hall, which opened later in 1421 AH. According to discoveries and excavations carried out in the region, there are more than 400 important archaeological sites across the Eastern Province, such as Dhahran, Tarut, Qatif, Jubail, Al-Ahsa, Khobar, Dammam, Thaj, Yabrin, Buqayq and others. These antiquities can be seen in the museum's six halls, displayed in special cabinets arranged chronologically from the Stone Age to the heritage of the forefathers.

60121434.t: Mohammed bin Abdul Wahab Palace Fort
60121434.s: Mohammed bin Abdul Wahab Al Faihani Palace, or Al Faihani Palace, is an archaeological palace next to a fort known as Darin Fort. It is in the village of Darin on Tarut Island in Qatif Governorate in eastern Saudi Arabia. The fort was restored by Mohammed bin Abdul Wahab Al Faihani between 1884 and 1885, after which it became known by his name.
60121434.b:
Mohammed bin Abdul Wahab Al Faihani Palace, or Al Faihani Palace, is an archaeological palace next to a fort known as Darin Fort. It is in the village of Darin on Tarut Island in Qatif Governorate in eastern Saudi Arabia. The fort was restored by Mohammed bin Abdul Wahab Al Faihani between 1884 and 1885, after which it became known by his name.

The palace and its annexes stand in the middle of the curve of the coast south of Darin, and include several facilities and annexes: a group of rooms, storerooms, majlis rooms and a rear courtyard. Its walls include a series of arches designed in the Islamic Abbasid style, and its total area with its annexes is about 8,000 square metres.

The palace and its annexes sit in the middle of the village of Darin on a large rise near sea level, between Al Hawta and the Eastern district. To the south it is bordered by a small mosque on a rocky rise that slopes gradually until it meets the sea directly at Darin port; to the east by a group of houses and then Darin Grand Mosque; to the north by an open square; and to the west by an abandoned house. The hill on which the fort stands consists of accumulated sedimentary layers, each representing a different period of time.

Darin Fort took on great historical value during the First and Second Saudi States and also in the Ottoman period, but together with the palace annexes it has become ruins and heaps of stones as its walls collapsed onto one another, and only its foundations remain.

60121394.s: Ramlet Al-Bayda Beach, also known as Al Rafia Beach, is a seashore overlooking Tarut Bay, west of the Arabian Gulf. It runs from the end of the town of Darin to the start of the Sanabis sea, and is one kilometre long. The beach ground is firm, hard and flat because its sandy soil is saturated with water, and it is free of rocks and natural obstacles, which once made it a landing site for planes and helicopters arriving at Darin Airport, about 600 metres from the beach.

60121319.s: Murjan Island is a tourist island in Dammam in the east of Saudi Arabia, and the first artificial island in the Kingdom. It was built by Aramco in 1991 during the reign of King Fahd bin Abdulaziz. The island is about 1,800 metres from Dammam Corniche and is connected to it by a paved bridge. It covers 7,000 square metres and has the "Malwiya" tower in its centre, with its unique design.
